surface_case: Nora Vance, a twenty-nine-year-old audio and tape restorer, inherits her late grandmother Agnes Vance's shuttered seaside hotel and begins restoring the reel-to-reel tapes left behind there. The hotel appears haunted by one impossible room: a cold, locked room Nora cannot remember entering, where salt gathers in dry places and old recordings carry a child's voice saying her name. On the surface, Nora is investigating whether the hotel itself is holding a presence inside the salt room.
true_case: The child's voice on the tapes is tied to Nora's own erased childhood. When Nora was seven, she had a twin sister, Della Vance, who drowned in the hotel's tidal pool while Nora stood frozen and silent. Afterward, Ruth Vance and the family erased Della from photographs, memory, and speech to survive the grief, while Agnes preserved the tapes as the only remaining proof that Della existed. The salt room was Nora and Della's room, and its cold is not an attack but the shape of a sister edited out of the family, manifesting only through recorded sound until Nora can remember and speak her name.
core_question: What happened the summer Nora was seven, and why does every recording from the hotel seem to know a child Nora cannot remember?
emotional_question: Will Nora keep accepting the blank place her family made inside her, or will she choose grief, memory, and the unbearable wholeness of naming Della?
book1_promise: A slow gothic psychological horror mystery told in third-person limited from Nora's perspective only, with quiet wrongness in every chapter, a concrete partial answer every two to three chapters, and dread built through sound, memory, salt, cold, and family erasure rather than gore or shock.
book2_hook: On the last restored tape, beneath Della's voice, Nora hears a second child's voice that belongs to neither Nora nor Della. Agnes erased more than one child from the family record, and in the final seconds of the recording, the third voice says a name Nora has never heard as the salt room goes cold again.
book1_ending_type: closed central mystery with unresolved series hook
reader_payoff_book1: By the end of Book 1, Nora fully recovers the truth of the summer she was seven: Della was her twin, Della drowned in the tidal pool, Nora was present and froze, and Ruth and the family erased Della afterward. Nora restores the final tape at the tidal pool and says Della's name aloud for the first time in twenty years, choosing to grieve rather than keep forgetting. The reader receives the concrete answers to who the voice was, why the salt room stayed cold, why Nora had no memory, and why Agnes preserved the tapes.
